text:
Between the God who promises and the God who demands there is in Genesis 22 no reconciliation. The narrator sets the two beside each other and chooses neither. The reader is left where Abraham stands on the mountain, with the knife raised and the ram not yet seen. The question raised by the story admits of no answer, and that want of an answer is the only answer it gives; whoever reads the chapter with attention is himself put to the trial.

Genesis 22 is in this sense rather more a story about reading than about sacrifice. Its lesson is that the weightiest things are those which a writer leaves unsaid, and that what is withheld is what is given. Each gap lays its demand upon the reader, who must bear the burden of so spare a style: Abraham keeps silence; Isaac asks his question; Sarah is absent; the narrator neither explains nor comments.
